rulings.reason: Keep: PaO2/FiO2 205 +/- 54 mmHg at enrolment, whole cohort (Table 1; Results).
The article prints the journal as 'Intensive Care Med (2024) 50:2125-2137'; DeepSeek's value is what the paper shows.
The decremental PEEP trial was a procedure used to identify PEEPEIT-dPL, not a comparator condition; the only comparator step is PEEPTABLE from the ARDSnet lower PEEP/FiO2 table.

Every enrolled patient had an esophageal catheter inserted per protocol, and all 30 had complete step comparisons (only ScvO2 missing in 4), so 30 attempts is a well-supported derivation, flagged derived.
rulings.evidence: p. 2127 Physiologic monitoring; p. 2131 Results ('All the remaining variables were available')

rulings.reason: Neither code fits. The paper confirms position 'by the presence of cardiac oscillations and by an end-expiratory occlusion test' in spontaneously breathing PSV patients: an occlusion test against spontaneous effort is baydur_occlusion_test. GLM's dynamic_occlusion_test is for passive patients; DeepSeek's signal_quality_verification_only ignores the reported occlusion test. Co-author: code baydur_occlusion_test.
rulings.evidence: p. 2127 Physiologic monitoring; p. 2126 Study population (PSV, RASS -2 to 0)

rulings.reason: Timing from intubation is reported: 'Patients were intubated for 6 [3-9] days ... prior to study enrollment' (Table 1: Days since intubation, median [IQR] 6 [3-9]).
The interval is measured from intubation (6 [3-9] days), so the reference event is intubation, not enrolment.
A median of 6 days from intubation is beyond 48 h; the codebook's 'unclear' ruling applies only when timing is known solely relative to enrolment, which is not the case here.

PEEPEIT-dPL is the PEEP with the smallest difference between EIT collapse and overdistension; dPLdyn enters only as the pixel-compliance denominator, and no driving transpulmonary pressure target or limit is set. 'other' fits, as both reviewers coded the target strategy.
